about: scripts/perf-guard.py, small-project part: a cold haxeon build and haxeon check of tests/perf/small-project with the CLI built from the checkout, from no compile server running to the server's exit: the CLI's start and its project resolution, the server's start and the compile. Two modes, each with metrics of its own: vm_*, always measured, with haxeon-aot set aside so the VM runs the CLI's and the server's bytecode; aot_*, measured only when the CLI and compiler built ahead of time (haxeon-aot, haxeon dev aot) are current, which run the CLI and serve the compile, and skipped otherwise. The CLI's digest store is the guard's own, filled by an unmeasured build before the measured ones, each on a fresh copy of the project; the empty_store metrics measure one more build with it emptied. Measured on Linux x86-64; scripts/perf-guard.py --update writes the metrics that improved beyond their tolerance, --raise=METRIC=REASON one that is higher on purpose with its reason (raise_reason), in the commit that moves it. Tolerances are fractions of the value (tolerance) or counts (tolerance_abs).

vm_build_instructions.why: Instructions of every process the build starts on the VM, from perf: startup, which dominates a small project's build, and the compile. Compared only where perf is installed and allowed.
vm_build_instructions.raise_reason: the VM compiles the whole compile server at startup, and the server program grew 4.8% from a6e8ed9a1 to d0d30ce1c (module-sections writer and linking, query-engine kinds and frames, slice-3 walks, smaller steps over ~200 commits); measured back to back on the recording machine, where d1586e828 and a6e8ed9a1 still reproduce the old baselines within 0.4%; making the module sections the default adds no instructions; before that, the commits bisected for aot_build_instructions: ac8a1069b's KeyValueIterable typing of Map and Array for every program and d76d07a0f's collection after each compile's response, counted because the measurement runs until the server exits (VM not bisected separately)

vm_build_allocated_bytes.why: What the compile server on the VM allocated for the build (its worker allocations): deterministic for a given compiler and project.

vm_check_instructions.why: As vm_build_instructions, for a check, which types the project without writing a module.
vm_check_instructions.raise_reason: the VM compiles the whole compile server at startup, and the server program grew 4.8% from a6e8ed9a1 to d0d30ce1c (module-sections writer and linking, query-engine kinds and frames, slice-3 walks, smaller steps over ~200 commits); measured back to back on the recording machine, where d1586e828 and a6e8ed9a1 still reproduce the old baselines within 0.4%; making the module sections the default adds no instructions

vm_check_allocated_bytes.why: What the compile server on the VM allocated for the check: deterministic for a given compiler and project.

vm_build_empty_store_instructions.why: As build_instructions, with the digest store emptied first: the build that reads and hashes every input, the pinned Haxe and the compiler's sources among them. A regression guard.
vm_build_empty_store_instructions.raise_reason: Measured on the baseline's own commit 295885ed1 it is +3.2% over its recorded value on this machine now, with every other metric there within 0.6%: the rise is in what the empty-store build hashes outside the tracked tree, not in a commit; main is +0.6% over 295885ed1.

aot_build_allocated_bytes.why: What the compile server with haxeon-aot allocated for the build (its worker allocations): deterministic for a given compiler and project.

aot_check_instructions.why: As aot_build_instructions, for a check, which types the project without writing a module.

aot_build_empty_store_instructions.raise_reason: an empty digest store now hashes the installed compiler executable, so a replaced binary with the same source stamp selects a new compile worker
